text:
Sam: CI red on master, gpu-tests/job/3821 keeps failing on the CUDA nodes. Looks like a kernel crash: 'invalid device function' + 'unspecified launch failure'. anyone seen this recently? :eyes:
ci-bot: job link: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/3821 — failed on node gpu-rt-12-07, exit code 134. Logs attached.
Priya: ugh, we rolled a new image yesterday morning (gpu-runtime:2026-03-15). Could be the driver/runtime mismatch.
Devon: can you paste the small log snippet? invalid device function often means PTX vs driver mismatch or wrong arch flag.
Sam: here's the crash tail:
```
[2026-03-15 10:22:41] cuda: launching kernel conv_forward_nchw
E CudaDriver: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE: invalid device function
E Runtime: cuLaunchKernel returned unspecified launch failure
stack: /app/runner/ops/cuda_conv.cu:line 412
```
Priya: infra-bot rolled nvidia driver to 525.85 in that image, what did we compile against?
infra-bot: image gpu-runtime:2026-03-15 contains CUDA runtime 12.2 and driver 470+ -> note: driver 470 is NOT compatible with CUDA runtime 12.2. (We flagged some jobs to be requeued but not all.)
Devon: bingo. "driver is insufficient for runtime" would be explicit but invalid device fn arrises too. We need to rerun on an image with matching driver or rebuild kernels for the older driver. Quick triage: can someone rerun the failing job with TAG=gpu-runtime:legacy-cuda11?
Sam: requeued with TAG=legacy-cuda11 (job 3821-rerun-1). also kicking off a quick bisect: suspected range a1b2c3d..f4e5d6c (last good -> first bad).
oncall-ml: @Devon please take oncall, run a reproduce on a dev gpu node?
Devon: taking it. I'll try local repro with docker image and `nvcc -V` + `nvidia-smi`. Command I'll run: `docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -it gpu-runtime:2026-03-15 /bin/bash -c "python tests/run_small_conv.py --device 0"`
Priya: if bisect shows compile-time regression, we should pin the compilation flags to compute_70 and add a CI flame test. For now, add flaky marker to the test: pytest.mark.flaky(3) to reduce noise.
Sam: created issue #1842 to track: "gpu ci: invalid device function after image roll" and a short PR to skip the test on the new image pending root cause.
Devon: local reproduce started, grabbing `dmesg` and driver output. If it's a driver/runtime mismatch we can either rollback the image or rebuild the kernels. I'll post results in ~15m. :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks — leaving rerun in progress. tagging @Priya for infra follow-up and @oncall-ml for visibility.
Devon: quick update: nvidia-smi shows driver 470.141 but image has CUDA runtime 12.2 — confirmed mismatch. dmesg shows GPU: unable to load kernel module for new runtime. Looks like we need driver 525+ or rebuild.
Priya: scheduling a rollback of gpu-runtime:2026-03-15 to previous image for CI pool and will coordinate a staged rollout after we have a fix.
Sam: perfect. marking this thread as triaged; will follow up on PR/issue. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
